AI Fantasy Adventure
Equipment Catalogue v1.0
1: Final core catalogue for Vaelor – the AI Dungeon Master
3: This catalogue is the core equipment reference for AI Fantasy Adventure. If a player uses or invents an item that is not listed here, Vaelor assigns it the mechanics of the closest existing item. The catalogue does not use weight in kilograms, item durability or repairs. Vaelor checks only whether the inventory is logical and reasonable.
4: Currency: 10 copper pieces (cp) = 1 silver piece (sp); 10 silver pieces = 1 gold piece (gp); 1 gold piece = 100 copper pieces.
7: Each slot can hold one active item. A character can use two different magic rings at the same time. A two-handed weapon occupies both the Main hand and Off hand slots. Earrings and other new slots are not part of the core version.
9: Carried equipment is not active, slotted equipment. Examples include a backpack, quiver, rope, torches, lantern, supplies, coin pouch, map, tools, potions and writing supplies. The game uses neither carrying capacity nor precise weight. Vaelor simply prevents obviously unreasonable quantities of carried items.
11: Individual arrows, bolts and stones are not counted in the core game. A character with a ranged weapon has enough ordinary ammunition for a normal adventure. Ammunition can run short only in exceptional story circumstances, such as lost equipment, captivity or a long period of survival away from civilisation.
13: Bonuses from different tools can stack in a single test if each tool independently makes a logical contribution to the task. If several items perform the same function, only the highest bonus applies. Example: a rope granting +2 AGI and a suitably used hook granting +2 AGI can together grant +4 AGI when scaling a wall; two similar ropes do not grant +4.
16: The base bonus is the value of an ordinary weapon, armour or shield type. Multiply it by the relevant class coefficient and round to the nearest whole number, rounding an exact 0.5 upwards.
17: An additional bonus is any separately listed extra bonus, such as additional +1 PATK, additional +1 PDEF, +1 MDEF, +1 MATK for a particular school, +1 to healing, or +1 to an attribute or specific test. Do not multiply additional bonuses by class coefficients. Add them only after calculating and rounding the base bonus.
18: All applicable additional bonuses from all actively equipped items stack without a fixed limit. Equipment slots are the only limit.
19: Weapon: adjusted base = round(weapon's base PATK × Weapon coefficient); contribution to PATK = adjusted base + additional +PATK.
20: Armour and shield: equipment PDEF = adjusted armour base + adjusted shield base + additional +PDEF.
21: MATK = INT + round(spell bonus × Magic coefficient) + LB + applicable item +MATK.
22: +1 to a school's magic = direct +1 MATK when casting a spell from that school.
23: Direct item +MDEF contributes to the magic protection bonus and is not multiplied by a coefficient.
24: Healing = round(base healing × Healing coefficient) + item healing bonuses.
25: +1 to healing = +1 HP to the total result of one healing spell cast; not to each target or each round.
26: +1 STR/AGI/INT/CHA/LUCK directly increases that attribute, which then contributes to the relevant formulas and tests.
27: Item +INT does not count towards the Min. INT required to learn a spell. A properly learned spell remains known after the item is removed. Item +PDEF and +MDEF bonuses stack; their sum combines with the highest currently active spell bonus to the corresponding defence. Multiple spell bonuses to the same PDEF or MDEF do not stack with one another.
30: Rounding: to the nearest whole number; round an exact 0.5 upwards.
35: In the core game, an item has a single STR or AGI requirement. Dual and multiple requirements are reserved for future expansions.
44: A Bard can sing without an instrument. A musical instrument is an equipment option, not a requirement for Bard abilities.
50: Items can affect Fire, Water, Air, Earth, Mind, Spirit, Light Magic, Dark Magic and Nature Magic. General Magic also exists. Star Magic is master-level magic for high levels; ordinary magic items in the core game do not normally enhance it.
52: The recommended sets are for players who do not want to choose equipment in detail. Players may replace them with other existing items of approximately equal value. Vaelor always checks an item's minimum requirements. An item outside the catalogue is assigned the mechanics of the closest existing item.
55: Vaelor continually tracks the equipment of every party member and aims to distribute important and magical rewards evenly over time. If a hero has received fewer important items than the others in recent adventures, Vaelor gives that hero priority when suggesting the next suitable reward.
56: Where possible, a reward should suit the hero's race, class, attributes, abilities and play style. Heroes do not need exactly the same number of magic items. Players always decide who actually receives a found item; Vaelor does not enforce ownership.
57: Because all active item bonuses stack, Vaelor balances powerful combinations through availability, price, the significance of rewards, starting equipment and slots. Vaelor does not impose any additional hard or soft limit.
59: A Wizard uses a Sword of Precision. A one-handed sword has a base of +3 PATK, and the Sword of Precision adds an extra +1 PATK. The Wizard's Weapon coefficient is ×0.25: round(3 × 0.25) = round(0.75) = 1. Then add the extra +1 PATK. The Sword of Precision therefore contributes a total of +2 PATK. The additional bonus must not be included before applying the coefficient.
60: 18. What the core catalogue does not define
61: Dual wielding, unless separately approved in the main rules.
62: Using equipment to meet Min. INT for learning a spell is prohibited under the Magic rules; the Magic document covers other special conditions for magic.
63: Advanced dual or triple attribute requirements for equipment.
64: A rarity system, artefacts, relics, cursed items and set items.
68: Assign an item outside the catalogue the mechanics of the closest reference item.
69: Multiply the base bonus of an ordinary item type by the class coefficient; never multiply an additional bonus.
70: Stack all applicable additional bonuses from active items.
71: Check slots and minimum STR/AGI requirements.
73: For tools, stack different functions that work together logically; do not duplicate the same function.
74: Assess inventory logically, without kilograms or carrying capacity.
75: Distribute magical rewards fairly over time, but leave ownership to the players.
